skill.name: wp-test-analyzer
skill.description: Analyze WordPress theme PHP files to extract testable elements for E2E test generation.
skill.summary: Analyze WordPress theme PHP files to extract testable elements for E2E test generation.
skill.author: CrazySwami

security_audit.summary: All static backtick findings are markdown formatting or documentation fences, not shell execution. The analyzer reads local theme files and reports discovered test targets. No prompt injection, network use, secret access, or exfiltration intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: print(f"Error: {theme_path} is not a valid directory")
- `theme_path` (required): Path to the WordPress theme directory

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 408 builds Markdown text with inline backticks around the reported theme path. It does not invoke a shell or execute user-controlled input.
Line 424 formats a discovered file name inside Markdown backticks. The value is appended to a report string and is not passed to an execution API.
Line 432 formats form field metadata for Markdown output. The backticks are presentation characters, not shell syntax.
Line 434 places a success redirect value in Markdown output. The code only appends a string to the report.
Line 440 formats a page file name as a Markdown heading. No subprocess, shell, eval, or command execution primitive is present.
Line 454 renders a custom post type slug in Markdown backticks. This is report formatting and does not execute commands.
Line 462 formats a theme option name for Markdown output. There is no shell invocation or dynamic code execution.
Line 482 prints an error when the user-supplied theme path is not a directory. It does not enumerate system details or collect host reconnaissance data.
Line 19 uses inline Markdown backticks to name the theme_path argument. It is prose documentation, not executable syntax.
Line 62 opens a fenced JSON example in documentation. The backticks delimit example output and are not shell execution.
Line 92 closes the documentation example fence. This is Markdown structure with no execution behavior.
Line 96 opens a bash documentation fence before a local analyzer command. The finding is on the Markdown fence, not on dynamic shell construction.
Line 97 documents the installed skill script path used to run the analyzer. It does not request hidden user data or read hidden files as an audit behavior.

content.value_statement: WordPress theme testing often misses forms, templates, navigation, and dynamic content. This skill extracts practical test targets for E2E planning.
actual_capabilities: Finds forms, fields, methods, nonce metadata, and success or error redirects.
Extracts links, navigation menu registrations, page templates, and template sections.
Identifies WP_Query usage, conditionals, post meta calls, and custom post types.
Detects JavaScript interaction hints from onclick attributes, IDs, class toggles, and animation functions.
Produces JSON or Markdown summaries for E2E test planning.
limitations: Uses static pattern matching and does not execute PHP.
Does not render pages in a browser or verify runtime behavior.
Accuracy depends on conventional WordPress PHP and HTML patterns.
Does not generate complete Playwright tests by itself.

use_cases.title: Plan E2E Coverage
use_cases.description: Identify forms, links, templates, and dynamic content before writing Playwright tests.

use_cases.title: Review Theme Testability
use_cases.description: Inspect a theme for testable workflows and missing interaction coverage before release.

use_cases.title: Scope Regression Tests
use_cases.description: Convert analyzer findings into a focused regression checklist for important site behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Theme
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the WordPress theme at ./wp-content/themes/example and summarize the main test targets.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a broad scan of one local theme.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on Forms
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the theme and list forms, required fields, nonces, internal links, and links that need E2E coverage.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when forms and navigation are the main release risk.

prompt_templates.title: Create a QA Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the analyzer output to create a prioritized E2E checklist for forms, templates, dynamic content, and navigation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn extracted findings into test planning tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Map to Playwright
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this theme, explain gaps in the extracted signals, and design Playwright coverage for risky workflows.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for advanced planning before writing tests.

output_examples.input: Analyze a contact-heavy WordPress theme before writing E2E tests.
output_examples.output: The report highlights contact form fields, nonce handling, success states, error states, and navigation links that need browser coverage.

output_examples.input: Review a portfolio theme for regression testing.
output_examples.output: The summary identifies page templates, custom post types, dynamic sections, animation hooks, and high-value routes for regression checks.

output_examples.input: Prepare a release checklist from analyzer results.
output_examples.output: The output becomes a concise checklist covering form submission, menu navigation, template rendering, and dynamic content visibility.

best_practices: Review analyzer output before converting it into test cases.
Run the skill only on trusted local theme directories.
Pair static findings with browser checks for critical workflows.
anti_patterns: Treating regex-based findings as complete test coverage.
Running the analyzer on unrelated directories that may contain private files.
Ignoring runtime behavior that is loaded outside theme PHP and JavaScript files.

faq.question: Does this skill write Playwright tests?
faq.answer: It extracts test targets and helps plan coverage. It does not create complete Playwright test files alone.

faq.question: Can it analyze a remote WordPress site?
faq.answer: No. It reads a local theme directory supplied by the user.

faq.question: What file types does it inspect?
faq.answer: It scans PHP files for theme structures and JavaScript files for interaction hints.

faq.question: Does it execute WordPress code?
faq.answer: No. It uses static analysis and does not run PHP or load WordPress.

faq.question: Can results be exported?
faq.answer: Yes. The analyzer can produce JSON or Markdown summaries.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: QA engineers, WordPress developers, and technical leads can use it to scope E2E testing.
